answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a unique work verification mechanism that requires each identity to complete distinct projects graded by a jury of unrelated peers. For every new identity, the attacker must secure additional sponsorships, increasing the overall cost. As identities multiply, the evaluation time and effort compound, costing up to $5,000 per fake and consuming weeks of work. This forces attackers to create a hollow presence, like trying to light a cedar log beacon without enough kindling, making the endeavor increasingly costly and unmanageable.
